Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: The absolutive is the unmarked case in Chácobo. Full NPs follow ergative-absolutive alignment with the ergative marked by a high tone (=´) and the absolutive left unmarked (∅).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: Pronouns in Chácobo follow nominative-accusative alignment, not ergative-absolutive. The 1SG pronoun is 'i' in S/A function; accusative is marked by the suffix -a (epenthetic case formative). No ergative marking on pronouns.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: Same as GB409_2. All pronouns follow nominative-accusative alignment. The split is conditioned by nominal type: full NPs = ERG-ABS; pronouns = NOM-ACC.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: Same as GB409_2 and GB409_3. Pronouns are nominative-accusative across all persons.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs follow ergative-absolutive alignment. The ergative is marked by a high tone clitic (=´) on the NP; the absolutive is unmarked (∅). Example: hóni siri= 'old man=ERG' (Tallman 2018:106, ex. 3.1).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: No aspect-conditioned split is reported. The ergative-absolutive alignment on full NPs applies across aspectual contexts. Tallman (2018:32) identifies only two conditioning factors for the split: nominal type and post-clause-type/rank position.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Same as GB409_6. No split conditioned by aspect. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in perfective contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: No tense-conditioned split reported. Chácobo has a complex graded tense system (up to 9 distinctions), but none of these conditions the ergative alignment on full NPs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Same as GB409_8. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in non-past tenses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: No mood-conditioned split reported. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in indicative contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: No mood-conditioned split reported. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in imperative and hortative contexts as well.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: No realis/irrealis-conditioned split reported. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in realis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: No realis/irrealis-conditioned split reported. ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in irrealis contexts.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: No agentivity-conditioned split reported for full NPs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality-conditioned split reported for full NPs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: No animacy-conditioned split reported for full NPs.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: ERG-ABS alignment on full NPs applies in main clauses. The ergative high tone marker (=´) is attested in main clause declarative constructions ({A,S}-C order).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in complement clauses?
Comment: Not directly confirmed. The neutralization of alignment in C-{A,S} constructions (post-clause-type position) may affect subordinate clauses, but Chapter 7 details were not fully recoverable. Coded as uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in relative clauses?
Comment: Not directly confirmed. Same caveat as GB409_18. Coded as uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in adverbial clauses?
Comment: Not directly confirmed. Chácobo has a switch-reference system (D{A,S}) operating on {A,S} arguments in subordinate clauses, but whether ERG marking is preserved is not confirmed. Coded as uncertain.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in other non-main clauses?
Comment: Not directly confirmed. Coded as uncertain pending access to Chapter 7.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by other factors?
Comment: Positional neutralization: when the subject {A,S} appears after the clause-type/rank morpheme (C-{A,S} construction), the ergative alignment is neutralized, yielding perfect readings.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the genitive marker?
Comment: The ergative marker in Chácobo is a high tone clitic (=´), a prosodic/tonal marker, like the ergarive.

Feature: Is the ergative marker the same as the instrumental/comitative marker?
Comment: The ergative marker is a high tone clitic (=´). The instrumental and comitative are expressed by distinct morphemes in Chácobo. The tonal ergative marker is not the same as the instrumental or comitative markers.
